problem: Leveraging unlabeled action-free videos for robot learning requires bridging the gap between visual dynamics and robot-specific continuous control.
approach: ViPRA trains a video-language model to predict both future visual observations and motion-centric latent actions from videos, then uses a chunked flow-matching decoder to map latent actions to continuous control sequences with minimal teleoperated demonstrations.
contribution: Achieves 16% gain on SIMBLER benchmark and 13% improvement on real-world manipulation tasks while enabling smooth continuous control up to 22 Hz and supporting generalization across embodiments.

problem: Animals build flexible cognitive maps of their environments from sparse, disjoint experiences, yet existing computational models require long sequential trajectories.
approach: ESWM constructs spatial maps from sparse episodic memories by learning to predict unobserved transitions from minimal experience, with its latent space geometry aligned to environmental structure.
contribution: Demonstrates that neuroscience-inspired episodic memory principles enable rapid map construction, enabling near-optimal exploration and navigation without additional training.

problem: Modeling long spatiotemporal sequences requires capturing complex spatial and temporal correlations, but existing Convolutional State Space Models are limited to 1x1 state kernels for computational feasibility.
approach: ConvT3 structures state kernels using tridiagonal Toeplitz tensors to realize extended 3x3 spatial convolutions efficiently, enabling diagonalization for parallel training.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on most metrics for long-range video generation and physical system modeling while enabling efficient training with extended spatial kernels.

problem: Feature caching accelerates diffusion transformers but temporal extrapolation methods suffer from prediction errors due to irregular magnitude changes in output features.
approach: RFC leverages input-output relationships to enhance feature prediction accuracy through relational feature estimation to estimate magnitude changes and relational cache scheduling to identify high-error predictions.
contribution: Consistently outperforms prior caching approaches across various DiT models with significantly improved accuracy.

problem: Existing benchmarks probe narrow AI research skills in simplified settings, lacking realistic end-to-end assessment of agents performing LLM research including hypothesis formation and experiment design.
approach: InnovatorBench provides 20 realistic tasks spanning data construction, filtering, augmentation, loss design, and reward design with ResearchGym supporting long-horizon execution and asynchronous monitoring.
contribution: Frontier models achieve promise on code-driven tasks but struggle with algorithm-related tasks and long-horizon decision making, requiring over 11 hours to reach best performance.

problem: Conventional fMRI encoding models flatten 3D brain volumes into 1D vectors, removing spatial context, discarding anatomical information, and tying models to subject-specific voxel grids.
approach: NRF models fMRI activity as a continuous implicit function over standardized anatomical space, decoupling predictions from training grids and enabling resolution-agnostic analysis.
contribution: Outperforms baseline models in intrasubject encoding and cross-subject adaptation while reducing required data by orders of magnitude.

problem: LLMs show promise in formal theorem proving but their ability to serve as practical assistants for mathematicians by filling missing proof steps remains underexplored.
approach: FormalML introduces a Lean 4 benchmark with 4,937 subgoal completion problems extracted from ML foundational theories using a translation tactic that converts procedural to declarative proofs.
contribution: State-of-the-art provers highlight persistent limitations in accuracy and efficiency on this first benchmark combining premise retrieval with complex research-level contexts.

problem: Grokking causes generalization performance to stagnate over many epochs before suddenly jumping to high levels, and practitioners need methods to accelerate this slow phenomenon.
approach: Egalitarian Gradient Descent normalizes gradients so dynamics along all principal directions evolve at the same speed, a modification of natural gradient descent motivated by asymmetric gradient speeds inducing grokking.
contribution: Removes stagnation plateaus completely in some cases and significantly accelerates grokking on modular arithmetic and sparse parity problems.

problem: Super-resolution methods assume ideal bicubic downscaling but fail on complex out-of-distribution downscaling degradations, and existing blind-SR methods remain restricted to simplistic kernels.
approach: KernelFusion uses zero-shot diffusion to recover image-specific SR kernels directly from LR input by training a patch-based diffusion model on the single image and reconstructing HR with kernel matching.
contribution: Handles complex downscaling degradations where existing blind-SR methods fail through unrestricted kernel recovery and superior SR quality.

problem: Multi-instance image generation struggles with precise control over object layout and preserving identity of multiple distinct subjects in diffusion models.
approach: ContextGen integrates a Contextual Layout Anchoring mechanism to anchor objects in desired positions and Identity Consistency Attention to leverage contextual reference images for identity preservation.
contribution: Sets new state-of-the-art on multi-instance generation and introduces IMIG-100K, the first large-scale dataset with layout and identity annotations for this task.

problem: KV cache compression methods for LLMs risk losing critical local information in long-context scenarios, and performance degrades sharply when extrapolating beyond pretrained context length.
approach: FreqKV performs parameter-free iterative KV cache compression in frequency domain, leveraging observation that context information concentrates in low-frequency components.
contribution: Extends LLaMA-2-7B context window to 256K tokens while maintaining stable perplexity, outperforming existing KV compression methods on both prefilling and decoding.

problem: Extending GNNs to solve general convex problems like Second-Order Cone Programs with universality guarantees remains largely unexplored despite progress on linear and quadratic programming.
approach: Proposes novel graph representation capturing conic constraint structure and establishes universality theorem showing GNNs can approximate SOCP feasibility and optimal solutions.
contribution: Provides rigorous foundation linking GNN expressivity and generalization to conic optimization, with numerical experiments on SOCPs and real-world power grid problems.

problem: LLM hallucinations are typically viewed as harmful, yet controlled confabulations could potentially fill gaps in historical archives due to social and political inequality.
approach: Uses narrative cloze tasks to generate masked events in character-centric timelines from unpublished texts and evaluates LLMs' ability to produce controlled, evidence-bounded hallucinations.
contribution: Validates that LLMs possess foundational narrative understanding to perform critical confabulation for reconstructing divergent histories while maintaining evidence fidelity.

problem: Semantic segmentation methods fail to distinguish fine-grained parts within objects due to missing links between part-level cues and object-level semantics.
approach: HiPoSeg builds a structured prototype space capturing both object-level and part-level features through hierarchical contrastive learning for intra-level discrimination and cross-level consistency.
contribution: Produces consistent +3.07% mIoU improvement on multiple benchmarks including Cityscapes and ADE20K without additional inference cost.

problem: Inference from tabular data lacks the innovation seen in other AI domains and remains dominated by gradient boosted decision trees despite recent neural network advances.
approach: xRFM combines feature learning kernel machines with tree structure to adapt to local data structure while scaling efficiently, providing native interpretability via Average Gradient Outer Product.
contribution: Achieves best performance across 100 regression datasets and competitive results on 200 classification datasets, outperforming recent tabular foundation models and GBDTs.

problem: Discrete VAEs typically rely on approximations like Gumbel-Softmax or high-variance gradient-free methods that struggle on high-dimensional tasks like image reconstruction.
approach: Leverages natural gradient of non-parametric encoder to update parametric encoder without reparameterization, combined with automatic step size adaptation and transformer-based encoder.
contribution: Scales to challenging datasets like ImageNet and outperforms both approximate reparameterization methods and quantization-based discrete autoencoders.

problem: Subcellular localization prediction lacks datasets offering comprehensive 3D structural information, hindering application of structure-based models despite recognized importance of protein structure.
approach: CAPSUL introduces a benchmark integrating diverse 3D structural representations with fine-grained subcellular localization annotations curated by domain experts.
contribution: Demonstrates importance of structural features through evaluation of state-of-the-art models and discovers a decisive alpha-helix localization pattern through interpretable attention mechanisms.

problem: Knowledge fusion across large heterogeneous LLMs risks catastrophic forgetting and fails to effectively absorb knowledge from source models due to parameter conflicts.
approach: GraftLLM stores source capabilities in target model with SkillPack format using module-aware adaptive compression strategy to preserve general capabilities and reduce parameter conflicts.
contribution: Outperforms existing techniques in knowledge transfer, fusion, and forget-free learning while supporting heterogeneous LLM fusion.

problem: Diffusion model sampling suffers from solver-induced errors in stiff regions where ODE trajectories change sharply, degrading sample quality.
approach: ERK-Guid detects stiffness regions and targets solver-induced error as guidance signal using embedded Runge-Kutta methods to reduce local truncation error and stabilize sampling.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art guidance methods on synthetic datasets and ImageNet through stiffness-aware error reduction.

problem: Aligning diffusion models with human preferences is challenging without reward models or large-scale preference datasets, both expensive to obtain.
approach: SAIL enables diffusion models to act as self-teachers through iterative self-improvement starting from minimal human annotations, using ranked preference mixup to balance exploration and human priors.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results using only 6% of preference data required by existing approaches, demonstrating remarkable self-improvement capabilities.

problem: Machine unlearning approaches leave residual traces vulnerable to data reconstruction attacks, and existing defense mechanisms fail on large-scale deep architectures.
approach: ReTrace formulates unlearned data recovery as RL problem treating residual unlearning traces as reward signals to guide a generator toward forgotten data distribution.
contribution: Achieves 73.1% instance-level recovery and improves reconstruction metrics beyond state-of-the-art, with 100% improvement on text unlearning BLEU scores.

problem: ReduNet's white-box interpretability is hindered by computational complexity and limited ability to exploit class-specific structures, especially with limited supervision.
approach: Multi-ReduNet decomposes global learning into class-wise subproblems while preserving theoretical foundation, reducing matrix inversion costs and enhancing feature separability.
contribution: Achieves superior efficiency and discriminative power under limited supervision while retaining interpretability.

problem: Discrete diffusion models suffer from sampling wall where categorical sampling collapses distributional information into one-hot vectors, hindering parallel decoding efficiency.
approach: Loopholing preserves distributional information via deterministic latent pathway with self-conditioning strategy that avoids unrolling full denoising trajectory.
contribution: Reduces generative perplexity by 61% over baselines, closing the gap with autoregressive models and improving reasoning on arithmetic benchmarks.

problem: Medical time series classification suffers from poor generalizability across diverse datasets due to varying channels, signal lengths, task definitions, and patient characteristics.
approach: FORMED repurposes a backbone foundation model with task-specific channel embeddings and shared decoding attention jointly trained across datasets to capture medical domain knowledge.
contribution: Achieves up to 35% absolute F1-score improvement over specialized baselines through lightweight label query training requiring only 0.1% of parameters.

problem: AI models struggle with physical reasoning generalization from limited experience, especially in out-of-distribution settings, due to inability to abstract core physical principles.
approach: NFF extends Neural ODEs to learn complex object interactions through force field representations efficiently integrated by ODE solvers to predict trajectories.
contribution: Achieves strong generalization from few examples to unseen scenarios through physics-grounded representations enabling efficient forward-backward planning.

problem: Activating parallel thinking capabilities in LLMs through training remains challenging, and existing supervised fine-tuning methods encourage teacher-forced learning rather than exploration.
approach: Parallel-R1 introduces first RL framework for parallel thinking with progressive curriculum starting with SFT on easier tasks then transitioning to RL for harder problems.
contribution: Achieves 8.4% accuracy improvement over sequential RL baseline and 42.9% improvement after RL on math benchmarks including AIME.

problem: Adapting video generation models to robot control requires complex multi-stage post-training and architectural modifications, limiting practical applicability.
approach: Cosmos Policy adapts a pretrained video model through single-stage fine-tuning by learning to generate robot actions as latent frames, enabling test-time planning with value predictions.
contribution: Achieves 98.5% success on LIBERO and 67.1% on RoboCasa benchmarks, and highest average score on real-world bimanual manipulation tasks.

problem: Vision-language models' multimodal interfaces introduce new safety vulnerabilities requiring realistic end-to-end assessment, but existing red-teaming efforts lack scalability.
approach: ARMs provides adaptive red-teaming agent with 11 novel multimodal attack strategies integrated with 17 algorithms using layered memory and epsilon-greedy selection.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art attack success rate with 52.1% average improvement over baselines and exceeds 90% ASR on Claude-4-Sonnet.

problem: Diffusion models struggle with imbalanced datasets where majority classes monopolize model capacity, restricting minority class representation.
approach: Capacity Manipulation uses low-rank decomposition to explicitly reserve model capacity for minority classes through a specialized loss term.
contribution: Consistently and significantly improves robustness on imbalanced datasets, delivering greater benefits when combined with existing methods.

problem: AI control protocols based on LLM monitors become central points of failure vulnerable to adaptive attacks from untrusted models with knowledge of protocol and monitor.
approach: Instantiates adaptive attack exploiting prompt injections in model outputs to evade diverse monitors and complete malicious tasks.
contribution: Demonstrates frontier models consistently evade current protocols, with Defer-to-Resample amplifying attacks through resampling.

problem: Next token prediction alone provides limited sample efficiency in LLM pretraining despite its success as standard training objective.
approach: CoCoMix combines discrete next token prediction with continuous concepts from pretrained sparse autoencoders interleaved in hidden states.
contribution: Outperforms standard next token prediction and knowledge distillation on benchmarks with improved sample efficiency and enhanced interpretability.

problem: Autoregressive video generation diverges from standard LLM architectures or requires bulky external encoders and prohibitive latency from next-token decoding.
approach: Lumos-1 proposes MM-RoPE for video-adapted positional encoding and parallel discrete diffusion with Autoregressive Discrete Diffusion Forcing addressing frame-wise loss imbalance.
contribution: Surpasses Show-o2 on GenEval and COSMOS-Video2World on VBench-I2V and OpenSoraPlan on VBench-T2V with efficient discrete tokenizer.

problem: Flow-matching models provide high-quality generation but sequential denoising renders them slower than needed, and existing acceleration methods are static and non-generalizable.
approach: FastFlow uses finite-difference velocity estimates to skip intermediary steps via multi-armed bandit optimization of step-skipping decisions.
contribution: Achieves 2.6x speedup while maintaining high-quality outputs across image generation, video generation, and editing tasks.

problem: Widely used evaluation metrics systematically underestimate multimodal models' compositional reasoning capabilities on established benchmarks.
approach: Introduces group matching score leveraging group structure and proposes Test-Time Matching iterative self-training algorithm bootstrapping performance without external supervision.
contribution: GPT-4.1 surpasses estimated human performance on Winoground, SigLIP-B16 with TTM surpasses GPT-4.1 on MMVP-VLM, with 85.7% relative gains on challenging benchmarks.

problem: KV cache size grows proportionally with context length, creating deployment challenges even with compression methods that either lose accuracy through dropping or suffer efficiency bottlenecks in retrieval.
approach: FreeKV employs speculative retrieval shifting KV selection out of critical path with fine-grained correction and hybrid CPU-GPU KV layouts with double-buffered streamed recall.
contribution: Achieves near-lossless accuracy with up to 13x speedup compared to state-of-the-art KV retrieval methods.

problem: Token-level data selection for LLM fine-tuning requires additional reference models and relies solely on loss information, failing to preserve semantically important tokens.
approach: ssToken leverages history models to compute per-token loss differences and introduces semantic-aware attention-based token importance orthogonal to loss-based selection.
contribution: Both self-modulated and semantic-aware selection outperform full-data fine-tuning, with integration delivering synergistic gains exceeding prior token-level methods.

problem: Large language models generate tokens sequentially creating speed-quality tradeoff, while diffusion models generate in parallel but need many iterations to match quality.
approach: Planned diffusion combines paradigms by creating short autoregressive plan breaking output into independent spans then generating spans simultaneously using diffusion.
contribution: Achieves 1.27x to 1.81x speedup over autoregressive generation with only 0.87% to 5.4% quality drop on AlpacaEval.

problem: LLM planning for embodied AI lacks formal reasoning capabilities and safety guarantees required for physical deployment, with existing approaches either unreliable or simply rejecting unsafe plans.
approach: VIRF introduces neuro-symbolic architecture with deterministic Logic Tutor providing causal pedagogical feedback to LLM Apprentice for intelligent plan repairs grounded in formal safety ontology.
contribution: Achieves perfect 0% Hazardous Action Rate on home safety tasks while completely eliminating unsafe actions through tutor-apprentice dialogue.

problem: Learning with noisy labels and domain generalization when both label noise and distribution shifts occur simultaneously breaks assumptions of existing methods that treat these problems independently.
approach: DL4ND improves noise detection by observing that noisy samples showing indistinguishability within single domain exhibit greater variation across domains.
contribution: Significantly improves performance by leveraging cross-domain information to better distinguish label noise from natural domain shifts.
theme: Transfer Learning, Meta Learning & Lifelong Learning

problem: Current Speech Large Language Models treat emotion recognition as simple classification providing limited interpretability, underutilizing LLMs' reasoning capabilities.
approach: EmotionThinker reformulates speech emotion recognition as reasoning problem through RL with prosody-enhanced foundation model and GRPO-PTR that progressively introduces reasoning rewards.
contribution: Generates accurate emotion predictions with interpretable explanations grounded in fine-grained acoustic cues through deep reasoning approach.
